`app/actions.ts:5` uses `revalidatePath("/")` from `next/cache` — Next.js's recommended way to refresh the current page from a Server Action. It invalidates the route's cached data and re-renders the page on the same URL (no `redirect()`, no navigation).

`app/page.tsx:12` binds the action to the form's `action` prop. On submit, the action flips the value and calls `revalidatePath("/")`, causing the page to refetch and re-render the updated `enabled` state.

If the toggle affects data shared across many routes, use `revalidatePath("/", "layout")` instead to revalidate the whole segment.

part.text:
`app/actions.ts:5` uses `revalidatePath("/")` from `next/cache` — Next.js's recommended way to refresh the current page from a Server Action. It invalidates the route's cached data and re-renders the page on the same URL (no `redirect()`, no navigation).

`app/page.tsx:12` binds the action to the form's `action` prop. On submit, the action flips the value and calls `revalidatePath("/")`, causing the page to refetch and re-render the updated `enabled` state.

If the toggle affects data shared across many routes, use `revalidatePath("/", "layout")` instead to revalidate the whole segment.
